summary: Two Hood Politics episodes hosted by Propaganda: how the US antitrust ruling against Google's search monopoly echoes the 1998 Microsoft case, and how Rastafarian Zion differs from political Zionism and its colonial settlement of Palestine.

evidence.note: Evans introduces a compilation of two episodes of Prop's network show Hood Politics
News segment on the anniversary of October 7 and the destruction of Gaza
Sets up the Google antitrust case over search and ads
Microsoft's 1990s Windows bundling deals with PC makers
Netscape complaint and the DOJ case against Microsoft, Gates's testimony
Ruling that Google illegally monopolized search via default deals
Second episode opens: Rasta meaning of Zion versus Zionism
Rastafari origins in the 1930s around Haile Selassie
Rastafari reaches Jamaica through the descendants of the Atlantic slave trade
Herzl radicalized by the Dreyfus affair, proposes a Jewish state
Ottoman sultan refuses to sell Palestine; Zionists aware of Arab population
British takeover from 1917, partition and the 1948 founding of Israel

notes: Two unrelated Hood Politics episodes compiled, so subjects and themes are split; primary theme tech-internet is a coin toss against colonialism-imperialism. Covered span runs from the Dreyfus affair (1894) to the 2024 Google ruling; Solomon and Sheba folklore treated as background. Gaza war news (about 5 min) not vivid enough for mass-atrocity.
